title: 🔥 Why Did Jesus Say ‘My God, My God, Why Have You Forsaken Me?’
paragraphs: 🔥 Why Did Jesus Say ‘My God, My God, Why Have You Forsaken Me?’
"Imagine feeling completely abandoned. You cry out for help, but no one answers. Now imagine that in your darkest moment, God Himself seems distant. This is what Jesus felt on the cross."

📖 Matthew 27:46 (KJV):
"And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"

❓ READER QUESTION:
"Brother John, why did Jesus say this? Did God truly abandon Him? And what does this mean for us today?"

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal!
✔️ Why Jesus felt forsaken on the cross.
✔️ The deeper spiritual meaning behind His words.
✔️ How this moment fulfilled ancient prophecy.
✔️ What this means for us—how Jesus took our place!

DID GOD REALLY FORSAKE JESUS?
Many people misunderstand this cry from Jesus. Was He truly abandoned, or was something deeper happening?

📖 Matthew 27:46 (KJV):
"And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"
💡 THE TRUTH:

Jesus was quoting Psalm 22—a prophecy about the Messiah’s suffering!
He was experiencing the weight of our sin—being treated as if He were guilty!
The Father did not abandon Him, but allowed Him to bear the punishment in our place.
🚨 THE WARNING: Jesus was forsaken so that WE would never have to be!

THE DEEPER MEANING BEHIND JESUS’ CRY!
Jesus’ words were not just a cry of despair—they were a declaration of fulfilled prophecy!

📖 Psalm 22:1 (KJV):
"My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?"
💡 WHAT JESUS WAS DECLARING:

✔ 1️⃣ He Was Fulfilling Prophecy
🔥 Psalm 22, written hundreds of years before Jesus, described His crucifixion in detail!

✔ 2️⃣ He Was Experiencing Separation for the First Time
🔥 From eternity past, Jesus had always been with the Father—but now He felt the full weight of sin.

✔ 3️⃣ He Was Taking Our Place
🔥 Jesus endured the separation from God that we deserved!
🚨 THE WARNING: Sin separates us from God—but Jesus bridged the gap!

PROPHECY FULFILLED – JESUS’ WORDS WERE FORETOLD!
Jesus’ words were not random—they were part of God’s divine plan from the beginning!

📖 Isaiah 53:5 (KJV):
"But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed."
💡 PROPHECIES FULFILLED:

✔ 1️⃣ Psalm 22:16 – "They pierced my hands and my feet."
🔥 This prophecy describes crucifixion—before it was even invented!

✔ 2️⃣ Isaiah 53:3 – "He is despised and rejected of men."
🔥 Jesus experienced total rejection—even from those He came to save.

✔ 3️⃣ Amos 8:9 – "I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day."
🔥 When Jesus was crucified, darkness covered the land (Luke 23:44-45).
🚨 THE WARNING: If prophecy was fulfilled in Jesus’ suffering, then His return is also certain!

GREEK & HEBREW WORD ANALYSIS – DEEPER BIBLICAL REVELATION!
Understanding the original biblical words gives us deeper insight into Jesus’ cry.

🔥 GREEK WORD ANALYSIS – "FORSAKEN" (ἐγκαταλείπω – Eγkataleipō)
📖 Matthew 27:46 (KJV):
"My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken (Egkataleipō) me?"
💡 Meaning in Greek:

Egkataleipō means "to leave behind, to abandon, to withdraw support."
Jesus was feeling the weight of separation, but He was NOT permanently abandoned!
🚨 THE LESSON: God never truly abandoned Jesus—He was fulfilling His divine mission!

🔥 HEBREW WORD ANALYSIS – "SABACHTHANI" (שְׁבַקְתַּנִי – Shabachthani)
📖 Matthew 27:46 (KJV):
"Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?"
💡 Meaning in Hebrew:

Shabachthani means "to permit, to allow, to forsake."
Jesus was saying that God had ALLOWED this moment to happen for the salvation of humanity.
🚨 THE LESSON: Sometimes, God allows suffering—but always for a greater purpose!

PROOF & HISTORICAL EVIDENCE – JESUS’ WORDS IN REAL HISTORY!
Many skeptics question the historical accuracy of Jesus' words. However, both historical and biblical evidence confirm this event!

📖 Matthew 27:46 (KJV):
"And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"

🔥 PROOF #1: THE EARLY CHURCH CONFIRMED THIS EVENT!
❓ READER QUESTION:
"Brother John, how do we know that Jesus actually spoke these words?"

📌 The Gospels were written by eyewitnesses who recorded Jesus’ words as they happened. Early church fathers, such as Justin Martyr (100-165 AD) and Tertullian (155-220 AD), confirmed that Jesus’ cry on the cross was central to Christian belief.

🔗 Church Fathers’ Writings on the Crucifixion
👉 https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/
🚨 THE WARNING: If eyewitnesses and early Christians confirmed it, why do some people still doubt?

🔥 PROOF #2: ROMAN AND JEWISH RECORDS CONFIRM THE CRUCIFIXION!
❓ READER QUESTION:
"Brother John, do non-Christian historical sources confirm Jesus’ crucifixion?"

📖 Tacitus, a Roman historian (AD 56-120), wrote:
"Christus, from whom the name [Christian] had its origin, suffered the extreme penalty during the reign of Tiberius, at the hands of one of our procurators, Pontius Pilatus."
📌 This confirms that Jesus’ crucifixion was a real historical event—His words were spoken in a documented moment of history.

🔗 Tacitus’ Writings on Jesus – Roman Historical Records
👉 https://www.worldhistory.org/Tacitus/
🚨 THE WARNING: Even those who rejected Jesus recorded His crucifixion—so why do people still deny it?

POWERFUL PRAYER FOR TRUSTING GOD IN DIFFICULT TIMES!
This prayer is for those who feel abandoned by God and need to trust in His perfect plan.
🙏 🔥 PRAY THIS OUT LOUD:

"Heavenly Father, I know that even in my darkest moments, You are still with me. Just as Jesus felt forsaken on the cross, I sometimes feel alone—but I trust that You have never left me. Strengthen my faith and remind me that You are always working for my good. Help me to trust in Your perfect plan, even when I don’t understand. I surrender my fears, my doubts, and my struggles to You. In Jesus’ name, AMEN!"
